deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a printed library loan receipt (Leihschein) of the library of the Herzogliche technische Hochschule Carolo-Wilhelmina, Braunschweig, filled in by hand and signed by Dedekind.

Content: 'Fol. 1. 20.' The undersigned certifies that he has received on loan the following work. Verfasser (author/editor): Darboux. Titel: Bulletin des Sciences mathématiques, Série II, Tome III, November 1879. Braunschweig, 20 July 1880. Unterschrift: R. Dedekind.

Dedekind added a handwritten note at the bottom left: 'Seite 472: Anzeige von: Zolotaref, Théorie des nombres entiers complexes et son application au calcul intégral. Saint-Pétersbourg, 1874. (Par N. Bougaief.)' This refers to N. V. Bugaev's review of E. I. Zolotarev's 1874 Russian doctoral thesis on complex integers and its application to integral calculus. The pencil '2' at the right edge is the archival folio number.

Function in the bundle: the previous page (fol. 1v) is a German excerpt or translation of this same review. It describes the chapter on units (Dirichlet, Kummer, Kronecker; proofs via Hermite's bound for minima of quadratic forms). It then describes Zolotarev's chapter on ideal numbers, which starts from a monic integer polynomial F with F ≡ V^m V_1^{m_1}...V_s^{m_s} (mod p), where F = V^m...V_s^{m_s} + p F_1. The simplest case assumes F_1 is not divisible by any V_i mod p, with a promised transformation to reach this case otherwise. That is exactly the Kummer–Dedekind situation and the condition Dedekind analysed in 'Über den Zusammenhang zwischen der Theorie der Ideale und der Theorie der höheren Congruenzen' (1878).

The slip therefore documents when (July 1880) and where (Bull. Sci. Math. (2) 3, 1879, p. 472) Dedekind read about Zolotarev's competing approach. The excerpt on 1v was presumably written from this borrowed volume (my inference). There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Documentary evidence that Dedekind borrowed Bull. Sci. Math. (2) III (1879) on 20 July 1880 to read Bugaev's review (p. 472) of Zolotarev's 1874 thesis on complex integers, and excerpted it (preceding page).
results.modern_name: Reception history: Zolotarev's theory of ideals versus Dedekind's ideal theory (Kummer–Dedekind factorization of primes via factorization of F mod p)
results.usually_credited_to: Zolotarev (1874 thesis; 1880 J. Math. Pures Appl. paper); Dedekind (1871 Supplement X, 1878 Göttingen Abhandlungen paper)

deep.surprise_reason: Administrative document with no mathematical content. Dedekind's awareness of Zolotarev's work, which treats the same mod-p factorization problem as his 1878 paper, is known in the historical literature. The exact date and source of his reading is a minor but useful archival detail.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, discriminant; x=symbols('x'); discriminant(x**3+x**2-2*x+8, x) == -2012
checkable.asserts: Context only, not on this page: Dedekind's standard example of a cubic where the Kummer/Zolotarev condition fails at p=2 (common inessential discriminant divisor). The polynomial discriminant is -2012 = -4*503.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, factor_list; x=symbols('x'); factor_list(x**3+x**2-2*x+8, modulus=2)
checkable.asserts: Context only: the factorization of F mod 2 is x^2(x+1), showing the repeated factor V=x for which one checks whether F_1=(F - x^2(x+1))/2 is divisible by x mod 2.

transcription_corrections: The signature line 'Unterschrift: R. Dedekind.' sits on the same line as 'Seite 472:'. The handwritten note at the bottom left is 'Seite 472: Anzeige von: Zolotaref, ...'. The transcription's ordering splits this note.
The author's name is handwritten as 'Zolotaref' (single f), not 'Zolotareff'.
'Fol. 1. 20' is the printed 'Fol.' followed by a handwritten '1. 20' (loan register number). The '2' at the right edge is the archival folio number, not part of the text.
The handwriting 'Darboux' looks like 'Dapboux' due to the script. 'Darboux' is the correct reading.
